_readme: Punch list step 2 (2026-07-22): theory/progressions.md, transcribed as data.
Each entry is a feeling -> chord loop. `chords` is [[semitones from the
tonic, quality], ...], written the way the doc spells it (mostly A minor
or C major) but stored TONIC-RELATIVE so tools/harmony.py can drop the
loop onto any KeyContext by adding key.pc, same idea as key_context's
shift_from for MIDI phrases. quality is one of key_context.CHORDS.
roman is the doc's own spelling, for display only — not read by code.

sad_accepting.label: Sad, accepting
sad_accepting.why: Melancholy that keeps moving forward. It never lands hard on home, so it loops forever without feeling finished — that's why it can hold a whole song up.

sad_sinking.label: Sad, sinking
sad_sinking.why: The knife-twist. Sinks for three chords, then the last one brightens where you expect another sad one, right before the loop starts over.

uplifting.label: Uplifting
uplifting.why: The big triumph. Three bright chords with one sad chord in third place — the sad one is what stops it being sugar.

nostalgic_borrowed_minor.label: Nostalgic (borrowed minor)
nostalgic_borrowed_minor.why: An instant sigh. Plays a chord bright, then plays the same chord sad, then goes home; that one darkened repeat is the whole trick.

nostalgic_jazz.label: Nostalgic (jazz handshake)
nostalgic_jazz.why: Coming home, smoothly. Two chords that lean and one that arrives — the backbone of jazz, soul and lofi.

epic.label: Epic
epic.why: Stadium-minor, a slow march. Downhill and back up, wide, and it refuses to resolve.

dark_menacing.label: Dark/menacing
dark_menacing.why: Pure threat. Home chord, then the chord one single key above it — they don't belong together and your ear knows it.

dreamy.label: Dreamy
dreamy.why: Nothing tenses, nothing resolves. Two soft chords passing back and forth with nowhere to be.

vamp_i_iv7.label: Hip hop / neo-soul vamp
vamp_i_iv7.why: Room left for a voice. Two chords, never resolving, deliberately staying out of the middle of the track.

vamp_i_VI.label: Hip hop / neo-soul vamp
vamp_i_VI.why: A mood without demanding attention. Sad chord, warm chord, back again — the simplest loop that still says something.

vamp_ii_V.label: Hip hop / neo-soul vamp (never resolves)
vamp_ii_V.why: Suspense as the point. Two chords always about to go home and never doing it.

vamp_i_v7.label: Hip hop / neo-soul vamp
vamp_i_v7.why: Low-lit and still. Both chords are sad, so nothing brightens — it sits under a vocal without arguing.

trap_dark_metro.label: Trap dark-loop (Metro Boomin style)
trap_dark_metro.why: Dark, but always building. Three dark chords, then one brightened to lift the last beat before it loops; that lift is the whole illusion.

gfunk_minor_i_iv_v.label: G-funk minor (Still D.R.E.)
gfunk_minor_i_iv_v.why: A groove to ride, not a story. All three chords sad, moving in even steps.

vamp_static_riff.label: Static riff (no chord movement)
vamp_static_riff.roman: i (Am, held) - the riff/808 carries the melody
vamp_static_riff.why: Wide open on purpose. One chord, held — the riff and the 808 carry the tune instead.

emo_falling.label: Emo rap falling loop
emo_falling.why: Giving up, on a loop. Falls the whole way down and never climbs back, every chord lower than the last.

gfunk_dorian_9.label: G-funk Dorian bright-4 vamp
gfunk_dorian_9.why: The west-coast bounce. Sad home chord, but the second one is bright where it 'should' be sad — one wrong-in-a-good-way chord.

plugg_dream_9.label: Plugg dreamy 9ths
plugg_dream_9.why: Soft, hazy, half-asleep. Both chords have extra notes stacked on top, which blurs them.

horror_tritone.label: Horrorcore tritone
horror_tritone.why: Built to sound wrong. Home chord to the one distance the old church actually banned.

math_minor_thirds.label: Octave divided in four (minor-third cycle)
math_minor_thirds.why: Floats and unsettles at once. Four chords spaced perfectly evenly around the octave, so no chord is home and there's no gravity.

math_major_thirds.label: Octave divided in three (major-third cycle)
math_major_thirds.why: Dreamlike rather than happy. Three chords cutting the octave into exact thirds — bright, but it never picks a home.

math_whole_tone.label: Whole-tone climb (no leading tone, never resolves)
math_whole_tone.why: Weightless. A climb in even steps with the 'pull home' note removed, so nothing leans anywhere.

dorian_i_IV.label: Dorian's tell: minor tonic, MAJOR four
dorian_i_IV.why: Cool rather than sad. A sad home chord with a bright four — that combination is the whole tell.

harmonic_minor_i_V.label: Harmonic minor (raised 7th gives a major V)
harmonic_minor_i_V.why: Classical drama, and it lands every time. Minor, but the chord before home is sharpened so it pulls hard.

hijaz_cadence.label: Phrygian dominant / Hijaz — the Middle-Eastern cadence
hijaz_cadence.why: The Middle-Eastern sound, placed instantly. Falls onto home from the chord one key above — and home is bright, not sad.

noir_descend.label: Trip-hop noir — unresolved bVI-bVII cycle that never lands
noir_descend.why: Rainy-window music. Drops to a borrowed chord, nudges up one, then loops before it can land.

reggaeton_dark.label: Dark reggaeton — the documented dembow minor vamp
reggaeton_dark.why: Hypnotic, made to be danced to rather than listened to. Three chords walking down and around.

lydian_float.label: Dreamy (Lydian tell)
lydian_float.why: The floating chord. The second chord is bright where every other key would make it sad — that one raised note removes the pull home, so it hangs.

lydian_lift.label: Weightless lift
lydian_lift.why: Same floating trick with somewhere to go. Rises without ever landing hard.

lydian_wander.label: Dreamy wander
lydian_wander.why: Four soft chords drifting. Nothing tenses, nothing resolves — the long version of the two-chord dream loop.

mixo_vamp.label: Mixolydian vamp
mixo_vamp.why: Bright but not sweet. The second chord is one step BELOW home instead of the usual one below the octave — that flattened note is the rock and funk sound.

mixo_funk.label: Funk blues vamp
mixo_funk.why: All bluesy tension chords, no resolution. Every one is a stretched spring.

mixo_soul_climb.label: Soul climb
mixo_soul_climb.why: Steps down away from home, then walks back up. Warm, and it always comes back.

villain_harmonic.label: Villain (harmonic minor)
villain_harmonic.why: Classical menace. Two sad chords, then one BRIGHT chord where a sad one belongs, which yanks it home hard.

harmonic_climb.label: Harmonic minor climb
harmonic_climb.why: Drops to a warm chord then sharpens for the trip home. The sharpened chord is what makes it sound like a film score.

eerie_augmented.label: Eerie (parallel augmented)
eerie_augmented.why: Built to unsettle. The same uneasy shape slid up in even steps — no home note anywhere, which is exactly why it floats.

line_cliche.label: The melting line
line_cliche.why: One inner note creeps upward while everything else holds still. That crawl is the whole effect — dread in slow motion.

hendrix_snarl.label: Hendrix snarl
hendrix_snarl.why: The happy note and the sad note fighting inside one chord. That clash IS the funk snarl.

snarl_vamp.label: Funk snarl vamp
snarl_vamp.why: The snarl chord with a shove between hits. Aggressive without being fast.

suspended_open.label: Suspended, then resolved
suspended_open.why: Holds a chord that refuses to say happy or sad, then answers it. The wait is the point.

sparkle_add9.label: Sparkle
sparkle_add9.why: Plain major chords with one extra sparkle note on top — fresh, no jazz baggage.

anthem_sus.label: Anthem, unresolved
anthem_sus.why: Big and open, walking downhill, never landing. Made to sit under a voice.

power_stomp.label: Power stomp
power_stomp.why: No happy, no sad — just weight. Two-note chords hit like a fist because there's nothing in them to soften the blow.

soul_turnaround.label: Soul turnaround
soul_turnaround.why: The jazz handshake, then one more step past home into somewhere warmer. Four chords that actually travel.

gospel_walkup.label: Gospel walk-up
gospel_walkup.why: Climbs the whole way. Church music's engine — each chord one rung higher than the last.

neo_soul_descent.label: Neo-soul descent
neo_soul_descent.why: Lush and sinking. Every chord has extra notes stacked on it, so the fall feels soft instead of sad.

cinematic_rise.label: Cinematic rise
cinematic_rise.why: Minor, but climbing. Starts dark and opens out — trailer music's favourite four chords.
